mainTopic: Which animals אבר מן החי applies to (for Jews and for בני נח), and the כזית needed to be liable.
overview: The amud opens with an argument over whether אבר מן החי (a limb cut from a living animal) applies to non-kosher animals. רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר say yes, because wherever blood is forbidden, limbs are forbidden too. The רבנן say it applies only to animals whose meat is permitted. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה does not really need the פסוק, since for him one איסור can take hold on another. A ברייתא then lists three views: רבי אלעזר includes every animal and bird, the חכמים include only kosher species, and רבי מאיר includes only a kosher בהמה, based on "מבקרך ומצאנך". רב says the whole argument is only about Jews, while a בן נח is forbidden even from non-kosher animals. A ברייתא and a משנה about a non-kosher bird support this. Finally, רב rules that one is liable for אבר מן החי only for eating a כזית. The גמרא defends this against a challenge and then begins another challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר include non-kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר learn from the פסוק that wherever blood is forbidden, limbs from a living animal are also forbidden, so non-kosher animals are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The פסוק ends:] "And you shall not eat the life with the flesh." רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר hold: any animal whose blood you are commanded not to eat, you are also commanded about its limbs. These non-kosher animals too: since you are commanded about their blood, you are commanded about their limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק and explains how רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר read it. The blood prohibition and the limb prohibition go together, so wherever one applies, the other does too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "blood" (called the נפש, life) next to "the life with the flesh" (אבר מן החי). Since the blood prohibition applies even to non-kosher animals, they say the limb prohibition does as well. That is why they include טמאין.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut off an animal while it was still alive; forbidden to eat
The life; in this פסוק it refers to the blood and to the living animal
Commanded (here: commanded not to eat)
Non-kosher species

phrases.english: "And you shall not eat the life with the flesh."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:23. This is the end of a פסוק the גמרא began quoting just before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar hold:
Any animal whose blood you are commanded about
you are commanded about its limbs,
phrases.notes: "Its limbs" means limbs cut off while the animal was still alive.

phrases.english: and these non-kosher animals too:
since you are commanded about their blood,
you are commanded about their limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the source for רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר, which began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blood prohibition and the limb prohibition are linked, so since blood is forbidden even in non-kosher animals, so are limbs from a living animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבר מן החי applies to non-kosher animals as well as kosher ones.

steps.title: The Rabbis limit the prohibition to kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the פסוק as "eat the flesh alone," meaning after death. So the limb prohibition only applies to animals whose meat is permitted when slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: "You shall not eat the life with the flesh" means rather, eat the flesh by itself. Any animal whose flesh is permitted, you are commanded about its limbs. Any animal whose flesh is not permitted, you are not commanded about its limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוק. For them it only speaks about animals whose meat may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hear the פסוק as saying: don't eat it while alive, eat it only once it is dead. That instruction only makes sense for an animal you are allowed to eat after death. So non-kosher animals are left out of אבר מן החי.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh by itself, meaning once the animal is no longer alive
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Same פסוק, two readings: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר link the limb to the blood, which includes non-kosher animals. The רבנן link the limb to permitted flesh, which includes only kosher animals.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
"You shall not eat the life with the flesh"
but rather, the flesh by itself;
any animal whose flesh is permitted:
you are commanded about its limbs,
and any animal whose flesh is not permitted:
you are not commanded about its limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבר מן החי applies only to animals whose meat is permitted, meaning kosher species.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה need a verse at all?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה holds that one prohibition can take hold on top of another, the stronger limb prohibition should apply to non-kosher animals automatically, without a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, why does he need a פסוק? Let the limb prohibition come and take effect on top of the non-kosher prohibition, since the limb prohibition also applies to בני נח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: by his own rules, he should not need this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere רבי יהודה holds איסור חל על איסור, that a second prohibition can take hold on something already forbidden. The non-kosher animal is already forbidden, but אבר מן החי is stronger because even non-Jews are bound by it. So it should take hold automatically, and the פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does he need a פסוק?
A prohibition taking effect on something already forbidden
The prohibition of eating a non-kosher animal
Descendants of נח, meaning all non-Jews, who are bound by the seven מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that רבי יהודה is wrong. It is that his conclusion should follow from his own rule, so a פסוק looks like extra work.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, why does he need a verse?
Let the prohibition of a limb come
and take effect on the prohibition of a non-kosher animal,
since its prohibition applies to descendants of Noah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבי יהודה needs the source given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's use of the פסוק to include non-kosher animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under his own principle of איסור חל על איסור, the stronger limb prohibition, which binds בני נח, would take hold on a non-kosher animal anyway, so the פסוק seems unneeded.

steps.title: The verse is needed only for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that רבי יהודה does not need the פסוק. It is needed only for רבי אלעזר, who does not accept that a prohibition takes hold on an existing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. And when the פסוק was needed, it was for רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge: רבי יהודה really could manage without the פסוק. The פסוק is there for רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that a prohibition does not take hold where one already exists, even a stronger one. So without the פסוק he would have no way to forbid a limb of a non-kosher animal. The two Sages reach the same result for different reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees with the question)
Was necessary

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר agree that אבר מן החי applies to non-kosher animals, but only רבי אלעזר needs the פסוק. רבי יהודה gets there through איסור חל על איסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that two Sages who are listed together can share a ruling while relying on completely different reasoning.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
and when the verse was necessary, it was for Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר does not hold that one prohibition takes hold on top of another, so he needs the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by agreeing and moving the need for the פסוק to רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the questioner is right about רבי יהודה, and the פסוק serves the other Sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to be the source for both רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה relies on איסור חל על איסור. Only רבי אלעזר, who rejects that rule, needs the פסוק.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms that רבי אלעזר derives the rule from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records in רבי אלעזר's name that אבר מן החי applies to every kind of animal and bird, kosher or not, learned from the פסוק about blood. This supports the claim that the פסוק is needed for רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא: the ban on a limb from a living animal applies to domesticated animals, wild animals, and birds, both non-kosher and kosher, because the פסוק says "Only be strong not to eat the blood." Any animal whose blood you are commanded about, you are commanded about its limbs. Any animal whose blood you are not commanded about, you are not commanded about its limbs. These are the words of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support what it just concluded in Step 4. The person who uses the פסוק to include non-kosher animals is רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the גמרא said רבי יהודה does not need the פסוק, because for him one איסור can take hold on top of another. Only רבי אלעזר needs it. This ברייתא names only רבי אלעזר as the one who learns the rule from the blood פסוק, which fits that conclusion exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut off a living animal, which is forbidden to eat
Applies, is in effect
Domesticated animal, wild animal, and bird
Non-kosher species / kosher species
Commanded, here meaning under a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: In Step 1 the derivation was said in the name of both רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר. This ברייתא mentions only רבי אלעזר, and that is exactly why it supports Step 4.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
A limb from a living animal applies
to a domesticated animal, a wild animal, and a bird,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
as it says: "Only be strong not to eat the blood."
Any animal whose blood you are commanded about,
you are commanded about its limbs,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מְצוֶּּוה עַל דָּמוֹ –
phrases.english: and any animal whose blood you are not commanded about,
you are not commanded about its limbs,
these are the words of רבי אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of Step 4 with an earlier source
steps.raayaObject: That the derivation from the blood פסוק belongs to רבי אלעזר, who does not hold that one איסור takes hold on another
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that quotes the derivation only in the name of רבי אלעזר

steps.title: The חכמים limit the prohibition to kosher species
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים in the ברייתא hold that אבר מן החי applies only to kosher species. They read the פסוק as saying the meat may be eaten only on its own, after death, so the rule covers only animals whose meat becomes permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: it applies only to kosher animals, because the פסוק says "Do not eat the life with the flesh." You may eat only the flesh by itself. Any animal whose flesh is permitted, you are commanded about its limbs. Any animal whose flesh is not permitted, you are not commanded about its limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposing view of the חכמים. This is the source of the רבנן's reading that was explained in Step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the next words of the same פסוק. Meat may be eaten only once the life is gone, which assumes the meat is permitted after a proper slaughter. So the test is not "is its blood forbidden?" but "is its meat permitted?" That leaves out non-kosher animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher species
The life (of the animal)
The flesh by itself, without the life
Permitted

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
it applies only to kosher animals,
as it says: "Do not eat the life with the flesh,"
rather, eat the flesh by itself,
any animal whose flesh is permitted,
you are commanded about its limbs,
and any animal whose flesh is not permitted,
you are not commanded about its limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּטְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view inside the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבר מן החי applies only to kosher species, meaning animals whose meat is permitted after slaughter

steps.title: רבי מאיר limits the prohibition to kosher domesticated animals only
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds the narrowest view: אבר מן החי applies only to a kosher בהמה, not to wild animals or birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: it applies only to a kosher domesticated animal, and nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a third opinion. רבי מאיר says the ban applies only to kosher domesticated animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now three levels. רבי אלעזר includes every animal and bird, kosher or not. The חכמים include every kosher species, whether בהמה, חיה, or עוף. רבי מאיר takes the narrowest view and leaves out even kosher wild animals and birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher domesticated animal, such as a cow, sheep, or goat
Only, exclusively
Except, only

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on אבר מן החי: רבי אלעזר includes all animals and birds, even non-kosher ones (learned from the blood פסוק). The חכמים include only kosher species ("flesh by itself"). רבי מאיר includes only a kosher בהמה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
it applies only
to a kosher domesticated animal alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, narrower opinion to the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבר מן החי applies only to a kosher domesticated animal (בהמה), not to wild animals or birds

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's source?
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid and a list of uncertain names, the גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי מאיר's view that אבר מן החי applies only to a kosher בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: שמואל, שילא, שימי.) A statement comes down through רבה בר שמואל, or רבה בר שילא, or רבה בר שימי, from רב חסדא or רב יוסף. It asks: what is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks where רבי מאיר gets his narrow rule from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, רבי מאיר said אבר מן החי applies only to a kosher בהמה, and not to wild animals or birds. The גמרא now wants the source for this limit. The long list of names only records that people were unsure who said it; the content does not change.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that helps you remember a list (here, three versions of a name)
What is the reason? (asking for the source or logic of an opinion)
A limb cut off from a living animal, which may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the names. It is one statement, and the גמרא is just unsure who passed it on: רבה בר שמואל, שילא, or שימי, quoting רב חסדא or רב יוסף.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Shmuel, Sheila, Shimi.)
phrases.notes: These three names help you remember the three versions of the first rabbi's father's name in the next line.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel said that Rav Ḥisda said,
and some say it was Rav Yosef,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא
phrases.english: and some say: Rabba bar Sheila said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥisda said, and some say Rav Yosef,
and some say: Rabba bar Shimi

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: said that Rav Ḥisda said, and some say Rav Yosef:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of רבי מאיר's view stated in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק or reason that limits אבר מן החי to a kosher בהמה only.

steps.title: The source: slaughter from your cattle and your sheep
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's source is the פסוק that speaks of slaughtering from your cattle and your sheep, which are kosher domesticated animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your sheep."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that speaks only about cattle and sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cattle and sheep are kosher domesticated animals (בהמה), not wild animals or birds. This פסוק belongs to the same section as the blood פסוק used for אבר מן החי. רבי מאיר therefore limits the prohibition to the kind of animal this פסוק names.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall slaughter
Cattle
Sheep and goats (flock animals)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's narrow view comes from "מבקרך ומצאנך": only kosher domesticated animals are included.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your sheep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about slaughtering from cattle and sheep limits the prohibition to kosher domesticated animals.

steps.title: The argument is only about Jews; for בני נח everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב says the argument about non-kosher animals is only about Jews. A בן נח is forbidden to eat אבר מן החי from both non-kosher and kosher animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: The argument is about Jews. But for a בן נח, everyone agrees he is forbidden on non-kosher animals just as on kosher ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a new rule that limits the whole argument. It only applies to Jews; for non-Jews there is no argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opinions above argued about whether a Jew is forbidden to eat אבר מן החי from non-kosher animals. רב says this doubt does not exist for a בן נח. For him, the prohibition covers every animal, kosher or not.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument or dispute between opinions
A descendant of נח, meaning a non-Jew, who is bound by the seven מצוות בני נח
Everyone agrees
Warned, meaning forbidden by a prohibition
Non-kosher species / kosher species

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about which animals are included applies only to Jews. For a בן נח, אבר מן החי is forbidden from every animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Here טמאין and טהורין mean non-kosher and kosher species of animals. They are not about ritual purity.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the בן נח prohibition is broader than the Jewish one here. The limits the תנאים argued about do not apply to non-Jews.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
The dispute is about Jews,
but regarding a descendant of Noah,
all agree he is prohibited
regarding non-kosher animals just as regarding kosher ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument of Steps 5 through 7 to Jews only and states the rule for בני נח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is forbidden to eat אבר מן החי from both non-kosher and kosher animals; the argument is only about Jews.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב גידל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that a בן נח is warned about אבר מן החי from non-kosher animals just like kosher ones, but a Jew only about kosher ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: a limb from a living animal is forbidden to a בן נח from non-kosher animals just as from kosher animals. A Jew is warned only about kosher animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing רב גידל said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל said the argument about non-kosher animals applies only to Jews, and that a בן נח is forbidden either way. This ברייתא says exactly that, word for word in idea, so it supports him.

keyTerms.meaning: Warned, meaning forbidden by a Torah warning
Non-kosher animals
Kosher animals
A descendant of נח, meaning a non-Jew bound by the seven מצוות בני נח

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
A limb from a living animal:
a descendant of Noah is warned about it
for non-kosher animals just like for kosher ones,
but a Jew is not warned
except about kosher ones only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב גידל's statement from Step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב גידל's rule that a בן נח is forbidden in אבר מן החי from both non-kosher and kosher animals.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states this distinction between a בן נח and a Jew explicitly.

steps.title: Two versions of the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: Some read the ברייתא as 'טהורה' (singular), matching רבי מאיר; others read 'טהורים' (plural), matching the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the ברייתא reads 'kosher one' (singular), and it follows רבי מאיר. Some say it reads 'kosher ones' (plural), and it follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain which opinion the ברייתא follows about Jews, based on two versions of one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular 'טהורה' points to a kosher בהמה only, which is רבי מאיר's view from Step 7. The plural 'טהורים' includes kosher wild animals and birds too, which is the רבנן's view from Step 6. Either way, the part about a בן נח stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher one (singular), referring to a kosher domesticated animal

steps.confusionAlert: This argument is only about which animals a Jew is warned about. It does not change the main point that a בן נח is forbidden even from non-kosher animals.

phrases.english: There are those who say the wording is "a kosher one,"
phrases.notes: Singular, like the word for a kosher בהמה, so it only covers domesticated animals.

phrases.english: and it follows רבי מאיר.
There are those who say the wording is "kosher ones,"
and it follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies which earlier opinion the ברייתא of Step 11 matches regarding Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא reads either 'טהורה' and follows רבי מאיר, or 'טהורים' and follows the רבנן.

steps.title: רב שיזבי brings a proof from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי cites a משנה: one who ate a limb from a living non-kosher bird does not get forty lashes, and slaughter does not make it pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said: We also learned this in a משנה. If one ate a limb from a living one of it, he does not get forty lashes, and slaughter does not purify it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי quotes a משנה that he will use to prove רב גידל's rule. This step sets up the proof, and the next steps explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is talking about a non-kosher bird. It says two things: eating its limb does not bring lashes, and slaughter does not 'purify' it, meaning slaughter does not make it permitted. רב שיזבי will now ask who the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it, meaning a משנה also teaches this
Receives forty lashes
Kosher slaughter
Purifies it, here meaning makes it permitted

phrases.english: רב שיזבי said:
We too have learned it in a משנה:
If one ate a limb from a living one of it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the non-kosher bird the משנה is discussing (טהרות 1:3).

phrases.english: he does not receive forty lashes,
and slaughter does not purify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second support for רב גידל, this time from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב גידל's rule that a בן נח is forbidden in אבר מן החי even from non-kosher creatures.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in טהרות about eating a limb from a living non-kosher bird.

steps.title: Who is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי asks who the משנה refers to. It can't be a Jew, because for a Jew it is obvious that slaughter doesn't help a non-kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: About whom is it speaking? If you say it is about a Jew, it is obvious that slaughter does not purify it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי asks who the משנה is about, and rules out the option that it is about a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew, a non-kosher bird is forbidden no matter what, so obviously slaughter can't make it permitted. A משנה would not bother teaching something that obvious, so it must be talking about someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: About what case, meaning who is this talking about?
If you say, introducing a suggestion that will be rejected
It is obvious

phrases.english: About whom is it speaking?
If you say it is about a Jew,
it is obvious that slaughter does not purify it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing the משנה from Step 13 by asking who it refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה is speaking about a Jew or a בן נח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not a Jew, since for a Jew the ruling would be obvious. The answer comes in the next step.

steps.title: So the משנה is about a בן נח, who is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must be about בני נח, which proves that a בן נח is forbidden to eat אבר מן החי even from a non-kosher creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not about descendants of Noah? This shows that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי concludes that the משנה is about a בן נח, and that proves רב גידל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that slaughter does not permit a non-kosher bird to a בן נח while the bird is still convulsing. This shows that the living-animal prohibition applies to him even for non-kosher species. Unlike a kosher bird, slaughter here does not permit it through the rule that what is permitted to a Jew cannot be forbidden to a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not, introducing the only option left
By inference, from this it follows

steps.whatToRemember: Both a ברייתא and a משנה support רב גידל: a בן נח is forbidden to eat אבר מן החי from both non-kosher and kosher creatures. The argument about non-kosher animals is only about Jews.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about descendants of Noah?
This shows that it is forbidden to them.
phrases.notes: Forbidden to a בן נח even from a non-kosher creature.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּבְנֵי נֹחַ, מִכְּלָל דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof begun in Steps 13 and 14 by naming the only remaining option.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה refers to בני נח, which proves that אבר מן החי is forbidden to them even from non-kosher creatures, just as רב גידל said.

steps.title: The first half and second half of the משנה seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש points out a contradiction between the first clause and the last clause of the משנה about a limb from a living non-kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש set the first clause of the משנה against the last clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a problem: the two halves of the same משנה seem to say opposite things. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause says there are no lashes for eating a limb from a living non-kosher bird, suggesting that אבר מן החי does not apply. The last clause says slaughter does not permit the bird while it is still convulsing, suggesting that the living-animal prohibition does apply. These seem to conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction (literally, 'throws' one text against another)
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Pattish
raises a contradiction between the first clause and the last clause,
phrases.notes: First clause: no forty lashes for אבר מן החי. Last clause: slaughter does not permit the non-kosher bird while it is still convulsing. One sounds like the prohibition does not apply, the other like it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה brought by רב שיזבי and checks whether its two halves fit together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the משנה about a limb from a living non-kosher bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause implies אבר מן החי does not apply to a non-kosher bird, while the last clause implies it does.

steps.title: First half is about a Jew, second half is about a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש resolves the contradiction: the first clause speaks about a Jew, the last clause about a בן נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he answers: the first clause is about a Jew, and the last clause is about a descendant of Noah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני בר פטיש answers his own question by splitting the משנה between two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew, the Rabbis limit אבר מן החי to kosher species, so there are no lashes for that prohibition here. For a בן נח, it applies even to non-kosher species, so slaughter does not permit this non-kosher bird while it is still convulsing. Each clause addresses a different person.

keyTerms.meaning: He answers (resolves the contradiction)
A non-Jew, bound by the seven מצוות בני נח

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew is warned about אבר מן החי only from kosher animals; a בן נח is warned about it even from non-kosher ones.

phrases.english: And he answers:
the first clause is about a Jew,
and the last clause is about a descendant of Noah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: רֵישָׁא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְסֵיפָא בְּבֶן נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: each clause refers to a different person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to be about the same person, so they clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is about a Jew and the last clause is about a בן נח, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: אבר מן החי needs a כזית
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that one is liable for אבר מן החי only for eating at least a כזית, because the Torah calls it 'eating.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A limb from a living animal requires an olive-size amount. What is the reason? 'Eating' is written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the minimum amount of אבר מן החי a person must eat to be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says a person is not liable for eating a limb from a living animal unless he eats a כזית. His reason is that the Torah uses the word 'eating' for this prohibition, and 'eating' in the Torah always means at least a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size amount, the minimum amount that counts as 'eating'
Eating, which in Torah law means at least a כזית
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rav said:
A limb from a living animal requires an olive-size amount,
What is the reason?
'Eating' is written about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי צָרִיךְ כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who is bound by אבר מן החי to how much one must eat to be liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for אבר מן החי requires eating a כזית, because the Torah uses the word 'eating.'

steps.title: If he ate a כזית, he should get lashes anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם challenges רב from the משנה: if the limb was a כזית, the eater should get lashes for eating a כזית of a non-kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם objected: 'If one ate a limb from a living non-kosher bird, he does not get the forty lashes, and slaughter does not make it pure.' And if you think we require a כזית, he should get lashes anyway because he ate a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם uses the same משנה to attack רב's rule about a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the משנה must be about someone who ate a full כזית limb. But eating a כזית of a non-kosher bird is already forbidden on its own and brings lashes. So why does the משנה say he gets no lashes?

keyTerms.meaning: Receives the forty lashes (the Torah punishment)
If it enters your mind (if you think)
Let it come out for him: he should be liable anyway for another reason

steps.confusionAlert: רב עמרם agrees there is no lashes for אבר מן החי here (a Jew is warned only about kosher animals). His point is that there should be lashes for a different sin: eating a non-kosher bird.

phrases.english: Rav Amram objected:
If one ate a limb from a living one of it –
phrases.notes: 'Of it' means the non-kosher bird from the משנה.

phrases.english: he does not receive the forty lashes,
and slaughter does not make it pure.
And if you think we require an olive-size amount –
he should be liable anyway because he ate an olive-size amount.
phrases.notes: An olive-size amount of non-kosher bird, which brings lashes by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's rule from step 18 using the משנה cited earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that אבר מן החי requires a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the limb in the משנה is a כזית, the eater should get lashes for eating a כזית of a non-kosher bird, yet the משנה says no lashes.

steps.title: The limb was mostly sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers like רב נחמן: the limb had only a tiny bit of meat, plus sinews and bones that together make a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said: it is a case of a tiny bit of meat with sinews and bones. Here too, it is a case of a tiny bit of meat with sinews and bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by explaining what kind of limb the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole limb counts toward the כזית of אבר מן החי together with its sinews and bones. But for the sin of eating a non-kosher bird, only the meat counts, and here there was only a tiny bit of meat. So there is a כזית of 'limb' but not a כזית of non-kosher meat, and no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny amount
Sinews
Bones
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: A limb counts as a כזית with its sinews and bones together, so it can be a full כזית of אבר מן החי while having less than a כזית of actual meat.

phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said,
it is with a tiny bit of meat, sinews and bones,
here too
it is with a tiny bit of meat, sinews and bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ בָּשָׂר גִּידִין וַעֲצָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's challenge from step 19, keeping רב's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case narrowly: the limb is mostly sinews and bones
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כזית limb means a כזית of meat, which should bring lashes for eating a non-kosher bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limb has only a tiny bit of meat; sinews and bones complete the כזית for אבר מן החי, but not for the non-kosher bird prohibition.

steps.title: Setting up another challenge from a different statement of רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'come and hear' and starts quoting another teaching of רב. It will use this teaching to test his rule that אבר מן החי requires a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to quote another statement of רב so it can test his rule about eating a כזית of אבר מן החי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 20, that the limb had only a little meat, saved רב's rule from the challenge from the משנה. Now the גמרא tries a new angle and brings a source from רב himself. The actual quote and the challenge come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut off from a living animal, which is forbidden to eat
An olive's size, the smallest amount that counts as 'eating'

phrases.english: Come and hear, for רב said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge from the משנה was answered in Step 20, the גמרא opens a new challenge to רב's rule in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that one is liable for אבר מן החי only for eating a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup suggests that another statement of רב may conflict with his כזית rule. The details come on the next amud.
